items.stem: Zuri Cosmetics, a UK exporter, sells a product for £50 to customers in the USA. The exchange rate changes from £1 = $1.25 to £1 = $1.12. Calculate the dollar price before and after the change, and explain the likely effect on export sales.
items.answer: Before: £50 × 1.25 = $62.50; after: £50 × 1.12 = $56.00. The pound has depreciated, so the product is cheaper in dollars and export sales should rise, depending on price elasticity of demand.
items.markingKey: £50 × old and new rates. [M1] for a correct formula/method with substituted values; [A1] for both dollar prices. Units (%, $, days, times) required for [A1]. Apply own figure rule (OFR) to later parts. [1] direction of change in demand explained.

The management team is divided. One manager argues that the threats of entering international markets outweigh the opportunities for small businesses. Evaluate this view and recommend a course of action. [10]
items.answer: Threats are greater for small firms, but low-risk methods such as online exporting can let them gain the opportunities.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "licensing"?
options: Allowing a foreign business to produce a product or use intellectual property in return for a fee
Falling average costs from producing and selling at larger scale across several countries
Differences in values, beliefs, language, customs and behaviour between countries that affect marketing
Adapting the marketing mix to suit each country's market
items.answer: Allowing a foreign business to produce a product or use intellectual property in return for a fee
items.markingKey: A. "licensing" is allowing a foreign business to produce a product or use intellectual property in return for a fee.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "economies of scale (international)"?
options: Falling average costs from producing and selling at larger scale across several countries
Using a standardised marketing mix in all countries
Allowing businesses in other countries to use a brand and business model in return for fees and royalties
Allowing a foreign business to produce a product or use intellectual property in return for a fee
items.answer: Falling average costs from producing and selling at larger scale across several countries
items.markingKey: A. "economies of scale (international)" is falling average costs from producing and selling at larger scale across several countries.

items.stem: A key advantage of a standardised global marketing strategy is:
items.answer: economies of scale in production and promotion
items.markingKey: economies of scale in production and promotion. One product and campaign cost less.

Starbucks entered India in 2012 through Tata Starbucks, a 50:50 joint venture with Tata Consumer Products.

Explain why joint ventures help firms enter unfamiliar markets. Refer to the extract or to another organization you have studied. [4]
items.answer: The local partner brings knowledge of the market, culture, laws and distribution, and shares costs and risks.
items.markingKey: The local partner brings knowledge of the market, culture, laws and distribution, and shares costs and risks. [1] for each relevant point identified and [1] for each point explained and applied to the case (2 × 2). Generic answers without application: maximum [2].

items.stem: Briefly explain why entering international markets can spread risk.
items.answer: If demand falls in one country, sales in others may continue, so the firm is less dependent on one economy.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: If demand falls in one country, sales in others may continue, so the firm is less dependent on one economy. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Distinguish between global marketing and local marketing.
items.answer: Global marketing uses the same mix everywhere to cut costs and build a uniform brand; local marketing adapts the mix to each country, which suits local needs but costs more.
items.markingKey: Global marketing uses the same mix everywhere to cut costs and build a uniform brand; local marketing adapts the mix to each country, which suits local needs but costs more. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Explain the difference between a joint venture and foreign direct investment.
items.answer: A joint venture shares ownership, costs and control with a partner; FDI usually means the firm owns and controls the foreign operation itself.
items.markingKey: A joint venture shares ownership, costs and control with a partner; FDI usually means the firm owns and controls the foreign operation itself. One mark for a correct account of each side; further marks for making the difference explicit (not two separate definitions).

items.stem: Briefly describe Walmart in Germany and explain what it reveals about cultural issues in international markets.
items.answer: Walmart entered Germany in 1997 and withdrew in 2006 after losses estimated at $1 bn; practices such as greeters and smiling rules did not suit German shoppers and staff. Applying home-country practices without adapting to local culture led to failure
items.markingKey: Context (Walmart entered Germany in 1997 and withdrew in 2006 after losses estimated at $1 bn; practices such as greeters and smiling rules did not suit German shoppers and staff.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail. Link: Applying home-country practices without adapting to local culture led to failure – remaining marks for explicitly connecting the example to cultural issues in international markets.

items.markingKey: Context (IKEA adapts some products, such as smaller beds and rice cookers in Asia, while keeping its flat-pack, self-service global model.) – 1 mark for accurate, specific detail.
